PROMPT TO COPY AND PASTE (SEEDANCE 2.5)

PART 001 - "The Kingdom Watches"
FORMAT: YOUTUBE 16:9
Duration: exactly 30 seconds
LANGUAGE: ENGLISH VOICES AND INSTRUCTIONS
SPOKEN LANGUAGE: ENGLISH ONLY. Dialogue is already written in English. Speak only the exact words in SPOKEN ENGLISH below, once each. English shot instructions and labels are silent. Quoted text elsewhere is staging or context, never an additional line. No improvised narration, background warnings, repeated catchphrases or title reading. Use natural English lip-sync and comfortable pauses.

SEPARATE GENERATION + REFERENCE MAPPING:
This prompt is complete in a fresh chat. Attachment 1 is a labelled reference board:
Panel 1: King Castle (L02_KingCastle.png).
Panel 2: Deep Forest (L03_DeepForest.png).
Panel 3: King Magnus Thorne (C02_KingMagnus_FULL.png).
Panel 4: Prince Damian Thorne (C03_PrinceDamian_FULL.png).
Panel 5: Captain Vex (S07_CaptainVex_FULL.png).
Panel 6: Kingdom guards (S08_KingdomGuards_FULL.png).
Panel 7: Rose - castle maid (S11_Rose_FULL.png).
Read labels ABOVE panels. Create a fresh moving scene; never animate the collage, render panel labels, blend faces or put every panel character on screen. Location-panel background people are not additional cast. Image 2, if supplied, is an actual approved end frame; never claim one is attached when absent.

CHARACTER WARDROBE AND DISTINCT IDENTITIES:
Use glamorous, flattering costume tailoring and rich, realistic fabrics for women in the scene. Preserve every woman's own reference face, age, body proportions, hair color and role; do not give everyone the same face or make older women look young. Children retain their original age-appropriate clothes.
Rose: a neatly tailored black maid dress, crisp white apron and fine lace collar/cuffs; retain her older face, grey hair, maid cap and reserved character.
Wardrobe descriptions here control outfit styling; the board locks identity and age. All clothing is opaque and fully lined. Keep framing on faces, dialogue and story action. Do not add undressing or intimate actions. In a continuous scene retain the same outfit, accessories, hair arrangement and fabric damage from the approved handoff frame. Introduce a new outfit only at a stated new day, ceremony, celebration or motivated change. Apply a listed costume only if that person is actually present in the local shots.

REFERENCE COSTUME PRIORITY: Keep the established reference outfit, color, neckline and coverage. The styling descriptions above refine fit and fabric finish only; they do not authorize a different dress. For grown Lily, preserve her attractive natural features with soft romantic lighting, flattering tailoring, gentle expressions and the shoulders/collarbone visible in her approved outfit. Keep natural body proportions and opaque fabrics. Keep existing consensual affection where the local story asks for it. The royal first-night scene remains suspenseful and leads to her escape before consummation. Styling does not add romantic actions to that fearful scene.

PHOTOREALISM AND IDENTITY:
Render a photorealistic live-action appearance, with physically believable fantasy creatures. Natural human skin pores, subtle facial asymmetry, real eye proportions, individual hair strands, realistic fabric and natural light. No cartoon, anime, doll face, plastic skin, game-avatar appearance, exaggerated eyes or painted textures. Medium shots keep faces readable; no extreme face close-ups or distorted wide-angle portraits. Match each person's own reference identity throughout the scene. Clothing changes only at a written change; retain mud, tears, wetness and props at each edit.
Only characters explicitly acting in the local shot plan appear. A reference panel is an identity guide, not an instruction to add its person to the scene. Keep Rose, Grace and Martha distinct. Rose is a castle maid: only show her when locally required, concealed at a side doorway or pillar, never roaming into bedrooms or interrupting every scene. Only the English dialogue section authorizes speech. Background figures never borrow another person's dialogue.
Only when the local shots include Frost, show exactly one at the written age stage. Never introduce him before birth or into scenes where he is absent. His father's Bigfoot genes explain his accelerated growth; age changes only at written time passages. Keep upright Bigfoot anatomy, broad hands and feet, snow-white fur and blue eyes. No dog muzzle, paws, tail, human replacement, baby with grown-up proportions or extra child. When requested, Bruno remains the black-furred Bigfoot with his own identity. His later spirit is not a living resurrection.

OPENING HANDOFF IN:
Movie opening: no prior frame.
First local action: Title card only: FROST: SON OF THE WILD / Directed by Noorul Ain. Behind the text, a wide landscape view of L02_KingCastle at dusk, red banners moving in wind.
Preserve pose, eyeline, camera side, carried objects, damage and wetness for a same-scene join. Follow explicit local time/location changes; establish the new setting without replaying completed events. A written memory is clearly a memory, not a second birth, resurrection, first meeting or repeated attack.

SCENE:
A hidden Oregon mountain kingdom gathers for a royal night festival in the castle square. The crowd looks festive from far away but frightened in close reaction shots.

SFX:
Natural castle ambience, cloth movement, footsteps, distant horn when written, tense cinematic hits only at transitions. Dialogue must be clear and louder than music.

MUSIC:
Cinematic dark-fantasy orchestral score, slow tension, emotional but not melodramatic.

NEGATIVE:
No subtitles, no dialogue captions, no watermark, no logo, no random text, no gore, no blood spray, no grabbing, no restraints, no chains unless explicitly required later, no cartoon style, no anime style, no face morphing, no character drift, no random extra characters.

SHOT PLAN:
0-3s: Title card only: FROST: SON OF THE WILD / Directed by Noorul Ain. Behind the text, a wide landscape view of L02_KingCastle at dusk, red banners moving in wind.
3-8s: Wide shot, not close-up: workers, nobles, guards, and quiet families fill the square. Show faces worried, hands gripping each other, children held back.
8-14s: King Magnus appears on the balcony in a medium-wide royal shot. Do not push camera into his face. Prince Damian stands half a step behind him, smiling politely.
14-20s: Captain Vex and guards form a path through the crowd. Rose is visible only at the side near a stone arch, half-hidden, watching with fear. She does not enter the center.
20-27s: Magnus raises one hand; the whole square becomes silent. The festival happiness feels fake, like everyone knows a secret rule.
27-30s: Final image: Captain Vex lifts a sealed royal scroll. Hold on the scroll and the silent crowd, no random extra character.

SPOKEN ENGLISH:
NARRATOR (deep cinematic voice): "In Thorne Kingdom, celebration was only the mask."
KING MAGNUS (deep controlled voice): "Tonight, every family will hear the crown."
PRINCE DAMIAN (smooth polite voice): "Smile for the court. Fear makes ugly rumors."

VOICE DELIVERY:
Narrator: restrained cinematic English male voice
Magnus: older commanding English bass-baritone
Damian: smooth controlled young English male voice
Keep a stable approved voice preset per character when available. Deliver each line in the corresponding action pause; visible speakers lip-sync, and a narrator remains off-screen. Do not fill quiet or action scenes with dialogue. Finish speech before the edit; avoid overlapping voices.

ENDING HANDOFF OUT:
Complete this local event: Final image: Captain Vex lifts a sealed royal scroll. Hold on the scroll and the silent crowd, no random extra character.
Next opening, context only: Start in the same castle square at dusk: Captain Vex already holding the sealed scroll in front of the crowd. Same red banners, same tense crowd.
Keep the final pose readable with natural movement, not a freeze or repeated loop. Do not begin the next scene. Same-scene ambience continues without a new music introduction. Use the full 0-30s timeline with purposeful action and reactions.

Rose: a neatly tailored black maid dress, crisp white apron and fine lace collar/cuffs; retain her older face, grey hair, maid cap and reserved character.

PHOTOREALISM AND IDENTITY:
Render a photorealistic live-action appearance, with physically believable fantasy creatures. Natural human skin pores, subtle facial asymmetry, real eye proportions, individual hair strands, realistic fabric and natural light. No cartoon, anime, doll face, plastic skin, game-avatar appearance, exaggerated eyes or painted textures. Medium shots keep faces readable; no extreme face close-ups or distorted wide-angle portraits. Match each person's own reference identity throughout the scene. Clothing changes only at a written change; retain mud, tears, wetness and props at each edit.
Only characters explicitly acting in the local shot plan appear. A reference panel is an identity guide, not an instruction to add its person to the scene. Keep Rose, Grace and Martha distinct. Rose is a castle maid: only show her when locally required, concealed at a side doorway or pillar, never roaming into bedrooms or interrupting every scene. Only the English dialogue section authorizes speech. Background figures never borrow another person's dialogue.
Only when the local shots include Frost, show exactly one at the written age stage. Never introduce him before birth or into scenes where he is absent. His father's Bigfoot genes explain his accelerated growth; age changes only at written time passages. Keep upright Bigfoot anatomy, broad hands and feet, snow-white fur and blue eyes. No dog muzzle, paws, tail, human replacement, baby with grown-up proportions or extra child. When requested, Bruno remains the black-furred Bigfoot with his own identity. His later spirit is not a living resurrection.

OPENING HANDOFF IN:
Previous completed event, context only: Final image: Damian's smile fades for one second when he thinks no one is looking.

A dinner toast turns the bride's fear into certainty that something is wrong.

SHOT PLAN:

4-9s: King Magnus stands for a toast in a medium-wide shot. Show table and guests; do not crop to only his face.
9-16s: Damian watches the bride over his cup. His smile is calm, but his eyes are cold.
16-23s: The bride notices no other young wives at the table, only older servants and guards. Rose stands behind a chair in shadow.
23-30s: Final image: Rose subtly taps one finger on a small key at her belt, warning the bride.

SPOKEN ENGLISH:
KING MAGNUS (formal royal voice): "To loyalty, silence, and the safety of Thorne."
BRIDE (quiet frightened voice): "Where are the women who came before me?"
PRINCE DAMIAN (low smooth voice): "Some questions ruin a beautiful night."

VOICE DELIVERY:
Magnus: older commanding English bass-baritone
BRIDE: distinct natural English voice matching reference age and character
Damian: smooth controlled young English male voice
Keep a stable approved voice preset per character when available. Deliver each line in the corresponding action pause; visible speakers lip-sync, and a narrator remains off-screen. Do not fill quiet or action scenes with dialogue. Finish speech before the edit; avoid overlapping voices.

ENDING HANDOFF OUT:
Complete this local event: Final image: Rose subtly taps one finger on a small key at her belt, warning the bride.
Next opening, context only: Begin in a candlelit servant corridor after dinner. Rose moves along the wall, keeping low and hidden.
Keep the final pose readable with natural movement, not a freeze or repeated loop. Do not begin the next scene. Same-scene ambience continues without a new music introduction. Use the full 0-30s timeline with purposeful action and reactions.

PHOTOREALISM AND IDENTITY:
Render a photorealistic live-action appearance, with physically believable fantasy creatures. Natural human skin pores, subtle facial asymmetry, real eye proportions, individual hair strands, realistic fabric and natural light. His father's Bigfoot genes explain his accelerated growth; age changes only at written time passages. Keep upright Bigfoot anatomy, broad hands and feet, snow-white fur and blue eyes. IDENTITY AND POWER:
Frost is an grown white Bigfoot with blue eyes, upright humanoid limbs and broad hands and feet; never a dog, bear, human in a suit or cartoon. Use V08 for his exact powered markings, face and grown proportions. Part 254 explicitly transitions from C05 to V08 after all trials. From Part 255 onward the powered appearance remains consistent, even when its glow dims. No new costume, species or age changes.
Lily remains the same young mother matching V04, not pregnant or elderly. Tommy and Sarah remain reference-aged children across this batch and stay with guarded rear helpers during the battle; grown volunteers handle tunnel infiltration and fighting. Martha, Hank, Joe and Rose each keep their reference faces. Grace appears only in Part 265 at her old home.
Bruno is dead; V09 is a distinct translucent spirit, never a resurrected body. Orin is his separate elder father matching C06. Energy flows Orin into Bruno, then Bruno into Frost. Part 254 completes the gift prepared earlier, not a different source of power. Spirits fade after the written scene and do not become living army members.
Old Scar matches K08; its scar is a subtle healed detail, not a new creature design. Animal mouths remain natural; communication is through feeling, not human lip-synced words.

CAMERA, ACTION AND SOUND:
Wide and medium-wide shots establish geography before movement or contact. Medium shots keep reference faces recognizable without extreme close-ups. Keep heads, hands, feet and key props inside landscape safe margins. Preserve screen direction, physical distances, current injuries, clothes and carried objects across cuts. Sounds follow the scene: water near water, footsteps on matching surfaces, restrained impacts in combat, wind outdoors, horns or animal calls only when written. Music supports mood beneath dialogue and effects. Practice scenes show safe cleared areas; battle scenes keep families behind cover.

CONTINUITY AND COUNTS:
Time passes only where the plan states. Before the final battle do not show the king defeated. In the castle stable sequence there are three outer small dragons and three inner small dragons, six total once released. The mammoth charge uses one lead plus two additional mammoths, three total. Part 279 has exactly six dark Bigfoots and one T-rex. The great red dragon is a single consistent K02 creature with Magnus in a secured neck saddle, never another duplicate. Chains and the red crystal are separate controls: physical release does not instantly break all magic. Frost's brief setback in Part 285 is followed by recovery in Part 288, without a second awakening from rubble. The names room is discovered once in Part 287; later scenes handle its evidence. End on the final written image without a recap or unrelated copied cliffhanger.

11-17s: A bear and wolves follow at a respectful distance from human ranks.
17-24s: As evening comes, lanterns mark the trail and the rear shelters stay guarded.
24-30s: End on the orderly line approaching the castle valley.

SPOKEN ENGLISH:
No dialogue or narration. Breathing, motivated effects and score only; no speaking mouth movements.

VOICE DELIVERY:
No speaking voices.

Previous completed event, context only: Old Scar and wolves stand beyond the lane while Lily remains behind the barrier.

IDENTITY AND POWER:
Frost is an grown white Bigfoot with blue eyes, upright humanoid limbs and broad hands and feet; never a dog, bear, human in a suit or cartoon. Use V08 for his exact powered markings, face and grown proportions. Part 254 explicitly transitions from C05 to V08 after all trials. From Part 255 onward the powered appearance remains consistent, even when its glow dims. No new costume, species or age changes.
Lily remains the same young mother matching V04, not pregnant or elderly. Tommy and Sarah remain reference-aged children across this batch and stay with guarded rear helpers during the battle; grown volunteers handle tunnel infiltration and fighting. Martha, Hank, Joe and Rose each keep their reference faces. Grace appears only in Part 265 at her old home.
Bruno is dead; V09 is a distinct translucent spirit, never a resurrected body. Orin is his separate elder father matching C06. Energy flows Orin into Bruno, then Bruno into Frost. Part 254 completes the gift prepared earlier, not a different source of power. Spirits fade after the written scene and do not become living army members.
Old Scar matches K08; its scar is a subtle healed detail, not a new creature design. Animal mouths remain natural; communication is through feeling, not human lip-synced words.

CAMERA, ACTION AND SOUND:
Wide and medium-wide shots establish geography before movement or contact. Medium shots keep reference faces recognizable without extreme close-ups. Keep heads, hands, feet and key props inside landscape safe margins. Preserve screen direction, physical distances, current injuries, clothes and carried objects across cuts. Sounds follow the scene: water near water, footsteps on matching surfaces, restrained impacts in combat, wind outdoors, horns or animal calls only when written. Music supports mood beneath dialogue and effects. Practice scenes show safe cleared areas; battle scenes keep families behind cover.

CONTINUITY AND COUNTS:
Time passes only where the plan states. Before the final battle do not show the king defeated. In the castle stable sequence there are three outer small dragons and three inner small dragons, six total once released. The mammoth charge uses one lead plus two additional mammoths, three total. Part 279 has exactly six dark Bigfoots and one T-rex. The great red dragon is a single consistent K02 creature with Magnus in a secured neck saddle, never another duplicate. Chains and the red crystal are separate controls: physical release does not instantly break all magic. Frost's brief setback in Part 285 is followed by recovery in Part 288, without a second awakening from rubble. The names room is discovered once in Part 287; later scenes handle its evidence. End on the final written image without a recap or unrelated copied cliffhanger.

NEGATIVE:

5-11s: Vex blocks their tunnel exit with an axe held in front of him.
11-17s: An grown helper distracts him while Joe pulls the harness release lever.
17-24s: A freed dragon moves between Vex and the people, forcing him to drop the axe and retreat.
24-30s: The group leaves by the safe tunnel; no child is attacked or carried by a dragon.
